entries.name: agentmemory
entries.use_for: Add searchable long-term memory to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other MCP agents.
entries.why: Hybrid BM25, vector and graph search returns top results only, saving context versus loading a memory file.
entries.summary: agentmemory captures session events through hooks, such as prompts, tool use and failures, and stores them for later search. It works with any MCP client plus a REST API, with a live viewer. It uses confidence scoring, lifecycle rules and a knowledge graph.
entries.best_for: Coding agents that forget context between sessions and need memory shared across tools.
entries.not_for: Default file storage suits one local user; several writers need Redis. On native Windows, only the Copilot CLI connect step is automated.

entries.name: ai-memory
entries.use_for: Share long-term memory across coding agents so you can switch from Claude Code to Codex mid-task.
entries.why: Works with more than twenty agent harnesses and passes typed handoffs between them.
entries.summary: Captures observations from agent lifecycle hooks, turns them into wiki pages at session end, and gives the next agent a short brief plus full-text, entity and optional vector search. Handoffs have an owner and are claimed once. A web console is optional.
entries.best_for: Developers using several coding agents who are tired of re-explaining the project.
entries.not_for: Single-agent users happy with built-in memory. It needs a server to run for cross-machine use and hook setup per agent.

entries.name: AnythingLLM
entries.use_for: Self-hosted RAG workspace with built-in vector DB, agents and a developer API
entries.why: MIT all-in-one RAG platform: document ingestion, many vector DB and LLM backends, plus an API and embeddable chat widget.
entries.summary: All-in-one self-hosted AI application for chatting with documents, using agents and building workspaces. Connects local or cloud LLMs and many vector databases, is multi-user and offers a developer API and embeddable chat widget; also ships as a desktop app.
entries.best_for: A ready-made private ChatGPT-over-your-docs with agents and API, without building RAG plumbing.
entries.not_for: A full application rather than a library; deep customization of the retrieval pipeline is limited compared with frameworks like LlamaIndex or Haystack.

entries.name: Chroma
entries.use_for: Store and query embeddings locally or as a server, with a few lines of Python or JS.
entries.why: Simplest way to get a vector store running: embedded mode for prototypes, client/server for production; default store in many RAG tutorials.
entries.summary: Open-source embedding database with a small core API (create collection, add, query, update, delete). Runs embedded in-process for prototypes or in client-server mode, with Python and JS clients and an optional hosted Chroma Cloud.
entries.best_for: Prototyping and small-to-medium RAG apps needing a simple local vector store with few lines of code.
entries.not_for: Less suited to billion-scale or heavy distributed workloads than Milvus or Qdrant clusters; managed option is paid (Chroma Cloud).

entries.name: cognee
entries.use_for: Turn documents and data into a queryable knowledge graph memory for agents
entries.why: Combines vector search and graph extraction (ECL pipelines) to give agents structured long-term memory; self-hostable.
entries.summary: Open-source AI memory platform that turns documents, code and conversations into a self-hostable knowledge graph combined with vector search, using ECL (extract, cognify, load) pipelines to give agents persistent memory.
entries.best_for: Agents needing structured long-term memory across sessions with graph plus vector retrieval, running locally.
entries.not_for: Heavier than a plain vector store; graph extraction adds LLM cost and complexity, so skip it for simple chunk-and-embed RAG.

entries.name: Docling
entries.use_for: Convert PDFs, DOCX, PPTX and HTML into clean Markdown/JSON for RAG ingestion
entries.why: IBM-originated LF AI project; accurate layout, table and reading-order extraction, the hard part of RAG ingestion.
entries.summary: Document parsing toolkit that converts PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, images, audio and more into a unified DoclingDocument, with layout, reading order, table and formula understanding and export to Markdown, HTML or JSON for GenAI pipelines.
entries.best_for: Ingestion step in RAG pipelines needing accurate PDF layout and table extraction, with integrations into the GenAI ecosystem.
entries.not_for: Layout and OCR models make it heavier and slower than plain text extractors; it only parses documents, not retrieval or generation.

entries.name: EverOS
entries.use_for: Add a portable, local-first memory layer to agents, stored as readable Markdown.
entries.why: Markdown is the source of truth, with SQLite and LanceDB indexes and no extra servers.
entries.summary: A Python library and memory runtime that stores conversations, files and agent trajectories as Markdown, then syncs local SQLite and LanceDB indexes for retrieval. Search can be scoped by user, agent, app, project and session.
entries.best_for: Agent builders who want memory they can read, edit and Git-version, without running MongoDB, Redis or Elasticsearch.
entries.not_for: Setups without an LLM provider key. Vector search and reflection need an embedding provider, and richer features need rerank or multimodal providers.

entries.name: Faiss
entries.use_for: In-process similarity search and clustering of dense vectors, CPU or GPU
entries.why: The reference ANN library from Meta; powers many vector DBs and is the default for local, embedded vector indexes.
entries.summary: Library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors, written in C++ with Python/numpy wrappers. Supports L2 and dot-product search over sets that may not fit in RAM, with some algorithms on GPU.
entries.best_for: In-process nearest-neighbour search, local embedded vector indexes and research or large-scale offline ANN with CPU or GPU.
entries.not_for: A raw index library, not a database: no built-in metadata filtering, persistence service, or auth; vectors are identified by integer IDs only.

entries.name: FastEmbed
entries.use_for: Generate dense and sparse embeddings locally on CPU without PyTorch.
entries.why: ONNX-based and small, so it fits serverless and CI; supports popular open embedding and SPLADE models.
entries.summary: Lightweight Python library for generating dense and sparse text embeddings locally using ONNX runtime, without PyTorch. Default model is a Flag Embedding BGE model and it integrates directly with Qdrant.
entries.best_for: Local or serverless embedding generation on CPU with a small install, including sparse models like SPLADE.
entries.not_for: Limited to the supported model list (open an issue to request models); no GPU-centric training or fine-tuning, for which sentence-transformers is better.

entries.name: FlagEmbedding (BGE)
entries.use_for: Use and fine-tune BGE embedding and reranker models for retrieval.
entries.why: Home of the BGE models that rank near the top of MTEB; includes training and reranking tooling.
entries.summary: Toolkit around the BGE family of embedding and reranker models for retrieval, with inference APIs for encoding text and tooling for fine-tuning and evaluation.
entries.best_for: Using or fine-tuning BGE embedding and reranker models for search and RAG, including multilingual retrieval.
entries.not_for: Research-oriented PyTorch toolkit with a heavier install; if you only need to run an embedding model, a lighter runtime may suffice.

entries.name: GraphRAG
entries.use_for: Build a knowledge graph from documents with an LLM and answer global questions over it.
entries.why: Microsoft Research reference implementation of graph-based RAG; strong for whole-corpus questions plain vector search misses.
entries.summary: Data pipeline and transformation suite from Microsoft Research that uses LLMs to extract structured knowledge graphs from unstructured text, then answers questions using graph-based context, including corpus-wide queries.
entries.best_for: Whole-corpus or thematic questions over a document set where plain vector search falls short.
entries.not_for: The README states it is a research project in maintenance mode with no new features; indexing is LLM-heavy and costly. Use LightRAG or similar for lighter graph RAG.

entries.name: Haystack
entries.use_for: Build production RAG and search pipelines with pluggable retrievers, rankers and LLMs
entries.why: Mature, modular RAG framework (since 2019) with explicit pipelines and integrations for every major vector store.
entries.summary: Modular framework for building RAG, search and agent pipelines with explicit, pluggable components: retrievers, rankers, generators and many vector store and LLM integrations. Includes agent lifecycle hooks and token tracking.
entries.best_for: Production RAG and search systems where you want explicit pipeline control and swappable components.
entries.not_for: More boilerplate than higher-level apps like AnythingLLM; Python only and you assemble the pipeline yourself.

entries.name: Hindsight
entries.use_for: Add long-term memory to an agent so it learns from past work, not only recalls chat history.
entries.why: Retain, recall and reflect operations with Python and TypeScript clients and an LLM wrapper.
entries.summary: Hindsight is an agent memory system focused on agents that learn over time. It offers a server, clients, embedded mode and integrations, with memory types, observations, mental models and banks. It reports strong LongMemEval results.
entries.best_for: You are building autonomous or conversational agents that must adapt to feedback over time.
entries.not_for: The README says it may be overkill for simple workflows like n8n flows. Benchmark claims come from the authors.

entries.name: hnswlib
entries.use_for: Header-only HNSW index for fast approximate nearest-neighbour search
entries.why: Canonical HNSW implementation by the algorithm author; used inside Chroma and many other systems.
entries.summary: Header-only C++ implementation of the HNSW algorithm with Python bindings, supporting insertions, updates and deletions for fast approximate nearest-neighbour search.
entries.best_for: Embedding a simple, fast in-memory ANN index directly in C++ or Python code.
entries.not_for: Just an index: no metadata filtering, query language or server; the README notes the current version is a release candidate. Memory-resident graph.

entries.name: Knowledge Catalog samples
entries.use_for: Learn from Google Cloud samples for building context and metadata retrieval for AI agents.
entries.why: Official-style samples for Knowledge Catalog (formerly Dataplex).
entries.summary: Tools, agents and samples that demonstrate Knowledge Catalog, an AI-powered data catalog and metadata platform that forms a knowledge graph of structured and unstructured data. The samples show context management, enrichment and retrieval.
entries.best_for: Google Cloud users adding business context to data for AI agents.
entries.not_for: Use without Google Cloud. It targets a paid Google service, and the README says it is not an official Google product.

entries.name: LanceDB
entries.use_for: Embed a serverless vector store in your app, backed by files on disk or object storage.
entries.why: No server to run; columnar Lance format handles multimodal data and scales from laptop to S3.
entries.summary: Serverless vector database built on the Lance columnar format. Stores and searches vectors and multimodal data from local disk or object storage with no server to run, aimed at AI/ML workloads.
entries.best_for: Embedded vector search in apps and pipelines that scales from a laptop to object storage like S3, including multimodal data.
entries.not_for: Embedded/file-based model suits fewer concurrent-server needs; if you want a standalone always-on cluster service, Qdrant or Milvus fit better.

entries.name: LEANN
entries.use_for: Storage-efficient vector index for local RAG on laptops
entries.why: MLSys best paper: recomputes embeddings on the fly to cut index storage about 97%, making personal-scale RAG cheap.
entries.summary: Vector index for local RAG that reduces storage by about 97 percent by recomputing embeddings on the fly instead of storing them. Aims to let a laptop index and search millions of documents; telemetry-free.
entries.best_for: Personal-scale RAG on a laptop where disk space is the constraint, for notes, emails and files.
entries.not_for: Recomputation trades storage for query-time compute; less suited to high-QPS server workloads. Newer, less established project.

entries.name: LightRAG
entries.use_for: Add knowledge-graph-based retrieval to a RAG system with incremental updates.
entries.why: Simpler and cheaper graph RAG than heavier alternatives, with a server, web UI and multiple storage backends.
entries.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation framework using graph-structured indexing and dual-level retrieval for deeper context. Supports incremental updates, multiple storage backends and ships a server with web UI.
entries.best_for: Graph-based RAG on a budget, especially over domain-specific corpora (legal, financial) needing relational context.
entries.not_for: Graph extraction requires many LLM calls at indexing time; for simple FAQ-style retrieval plain vector RAG is cheaper.

entries.name: LlamaIndex
entries.use_for: Build RAG pipelines: ingest documents, index them and query them with an LLM.
entries.why: The most widely used RAG-focused framework, with hundreds of loaders, vector store integrations and 2,000+ contributors.
entries.summary: Widely used RAG-focused framework with hundreds of data loaders, index types, vector store integrations and query engines for ingesting documents and querying them with an LLM. The company's focus has shifted toward LlamaParse document parsing.
entries.best_for: Building custom RAG and document-agent apps in Python or TypeScript with broad integration choice.
entries.not_for: Large API surface that changes often; the README says current company focus is document parsing (LlamaParse is a paid service).

entries.name: LLM Wiki
entries.use_for: Turn documents into a linked wiki that an LLM builds and keeps current, instead of re-running RAG each time.
entries.why: Implements Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern as a full desktop app with a knowledge graph.
entries.summary: A cross-platform desktop app where an LLM reads your documents and builds an interlinked wiki. It follows an ingest, query and lint loop with index and log files, wikilinks and YAML frontmatter. It parses PDFs, Office files and images, and works as an Obsidian vault.
entries.best_for: Personal or team knowledge bases that you want compiled once and kept current.
entries.not_for: Embedding retrieval into your own app. It is a desktop app, and its license is not a standard one.

entries.name: LongMemory
entries.use_for: Add durable, time-aware, governed memory to LLM apps and agents.
entries.why: Tracks what was true when, with provenance and scoped access, not just nearest vectors.
entries.summary: A local-first memory engine on SQLite. It keeps immutable content with provenance and separate recorded and valid time, plus a typed graph, decay and scoped permissions. Offered via npm, CLI, HTTP, MCP, a dashboard and VS Code.
entries.best_for: Agents that need memory that handles changing facts, multiple users or projects, and explainable recall.
entries.not_for: More concept-heavy than a plain vector store. Overkill if you only need simple similarity search.

entries.name: M-flow
entries.use_for: Build graph-based memory and retrieval that scores evidence paths, not just chunks.
entries.why: A four-level Cone Graph from episodes down to facts, with several retrieval modes.
entries.summary: A Python memory engine that organizes knowledge as Episodes, Facets, FacetPoints and Entities. It offers five retrieval modes, 50+ file formats, many vector and graph databases, many LLM providers, an MCP server, a CLI and a web UI.
entries.best_for: Agent or RAG apps where answers need linked context across documents, not isolated chunks.
entries.not_for: Summaries keep detail, so retrieved context is longer. Its benchmark claims are the authors' own.

entries.name: Mem0
entries.use_for: Persistent long-term memory layer for AI agents and assistants
entries.why: Most adopted agent memory layer: extracts, stores and retrieves user facts across sessions on top of vector and graph stores.
entries.summary: Memory layer for AI assistants and agents that extracts user facts and preferences, stores them and retrieves them across sessions on top of vector and graph stores. Offers a hosted platform and open-source library.
entries.best_for: Adding persistent personalization and long-term memory to chatbots and agents.
entries.not_for: Adds an LLM extraction step and storage to maintain; unnecessary for stateless bots. Some features are tied to the hosted platform.

entries.name: MemoryBear
entries.use_for: Give AI apps long-term memory that is extracted, linked in a graph and forgotten over time.
entries.why: Models memory as perceive, extract, associate and forget, instead of static retrieval.
entries.summary: An AI memory system from RedBear AI built on FastAPI and Neo4j. It follows a lifecycle of perception, extraction, association and forgetting, inspired by how brains encode and prune memory. It targets limits of context windows and static knowledge.
entries.best_for: Chat or agent products that need personalized memory across long conversations.
entries.not_for: Needs Neo4j and a multi-service Python deployment. The excerpt is research-heavy, so check benchmarks and fit before adopting.

entries.name: MemPalace
entries.use_for: Store your AI conversation history verbatim and search it later, fully on your machine.
entries.why: Keeps raw text instead of summaries, with a pluggable backend and no API calls.
entries.summary: MemPalace stores conversations as verbatim text and retrieves them with semantic search. The index is organized into wings (people and projects), rooms (topics) and drawers (original content). ChromaDB is the default backend and others can be added.
entries.best_for: You want long-term memory for agents or chats that stays local and never rewrites what was said.
entries.not_for: The README warns that Claude Code sessions expire in 30 days unless auto-save hooks are set up. Its official sources are only the repo, PyPI and one docs site.

entries.name: Milvus
entries.use_for: Run a distributed vector database for billion-scale similarity search.
entries.why: Built for very large collections with GPU indexes and horizontal scaling; Milvus Lite covers local development.
entries.summary: Distributed, Kubernetes-native vector database written in Go and C++ with CPU and GPU acceleration, designed for billions of vectors and real-time streaming updates. Milvus Lite covers local development.
entries.best_for: Very large-scale similarity search and production vector workloads that need horizontal scaling.
entries.not_for: Heavy to operate for small projects (many components); use Chroma, pgvector or Qdrant for modest datasets.

entries.name: Open Brain (OB1)
entries.use_for: Set up one shared database with vector search and MCP so all your AI tools use the same memory.
entries.why: A guided build of database, AI gateway, chat capture and MCP server, with extensions on top.
entries.summary: A setup guide and set of extensions for a personal memory layer: a database with vector search, an AI gateway and a chat channel such as Slack. Tools like Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Claude Code connect over MCP. It deploys as Supabase Edge Functions.
entries.best_for: People who want their own persistent AI memory shared across assistants without SaaS middleware.
entries.not_for: The license is not clearly identified in the metadata, so check the terms before commercial use. It is a guided setup, not a drop-in library.
keywords: persistent memory for chatgpt and claude

entries.name: OpenKB
entries.use_for: Compile documents into a linked markdown wiki and query it without a vector database.
entries.why: Builds knowledge once into a maintained wiki, using PageIndex reasoning-based retrieval for long documents.
entries.summary: A CLI that uses LLMs to turn PDFs, Office files, HTML, CSV and URLs into summaries, concept pages, entity pages and cross-links. Long documents use PageIndex tree indexing instead of vectors. You can query or chat, distill agent skills, and browse in Obsidian or a bundled web UI.
entries.best_for: Building a persistent knowledge base from long documents when classic RAG keeps rediscovering the same facts.
entries.not_for: LLM calls to compile and maintain the wiki cost tokens. Not a low-latency vector search service.

entries.name: OpenViking
entries.use_for: Context database unifying agent memory, knowledge RAG and skills
entries.why: ByteDance Volcengine project that organises agent context as a filesystem-like hierarchy with tiered retrieval; AGPL-3.0.
entries.summary: Context database for AI agents that organizes memory, knowledge and skills as a virtual filesystem under viking://, navigable with ls, tree, read and grep and with tiered retrieval. Developed by ByteDance Volcengine.
entries.best_for: Agents needing inspectable, hierarchical context where you can see and edit what the agent knows.
entries.not_for: AGPL-3.0 license limits use in closed-source network services; newer and less proven than mainstream vector stores.

entries.name: PaddleOCR
entries.use_for: OCR and document parsing to turn PDFs and images into structured data for RAG
entries.why: Mature multilingual OCR + layout/table parsing (PP-Structure) that feeds clean text into retrieval pipelines; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: OCR and document parsing toolkit that converts PDFs and images into structured JSON or Markdown, with multilingual text recognition and layout/table parsing. Models can be exported to ONNX and run on engines like OpenVINO and TensorRT.
entries.best_for: Feeding RAG pipelines with text from scanned PDFs and images, multilingual OCR, and layout or table extraction.
entries.not_for: Built on the PaddlePaddle ecosystem, so setup is heavier than lightweight OCR tools; only extraction, not retrieval or chat.

entries.name: PageIndex
entries.use_for: Vectorless, reasoning-based RAG over long documents via a tree index
entries.why: Builds a table-of-contents style tree and lets the LLM navigate it, a strong alternative to chunk+embed for long structured docs.
entries.summary: Vectorless, reasoning-based RAG that builds a table-of-contents style tree index of a long document and has the LLM navigate it, with no vector DB or chunking. The SDK has a local mode using your own LLM key or a cloud option.
entries.best_for: Long, structured documents (reports, filings, manuals) where chunk-and-embed loses context.
entries.not_for: Relies on LLM calls to index and navigate, so costs and latency are higher; best for structured docs, less for huge unstructured corpora.

entries.name: pgvector
entries.use_for: Add vector similarity search to an existing Postgres database.
entries.why: Keeps vectors next to your relational data with HNSW/IVFFlat indexes; supported by nearly every managed Postgres provider.
entries.summary: Postgres extension for vector similarity search. Supports exact and approximate (HNSW, IVFFlat) search with several vector types and distance metrics while keeping ACID, joins and point-in-time recovery.
entries.best_for: Adding semantic search to an existing Postgres app so vectors live beside relational data, available on most managed Postgres services.
entries.not_for: Not as specialized or scalable as dedicated vector DBs for very large collections; ANN index builds and tuning use Postgres resources.

entries.name: PixelRAG
entries.use_for: Do retrieval-augmented generation over page screenshots so tables and charts are not lost.
entries.why: Retrieves rendered page tiles with a fine-tuned vision embedding model.
entries.summary: Renders web pages, PDFs and images to screenshot tiles with the pixelshot command, then searches them with a Qwen3-VL-Embedding model tuned on screenshots. A Wikipedia index is prebuilt. It also ships a pixelbrowse skill so Claude can read pages as images.
entries.best_for: Documents where layout, tables and charts matter and text parsing breaks them.
entries.not_for: Plain-text corpora where normal chunking works fine. Image retrieval needs GPU-class embedding models and more storage.

entries.name: PrivateGPT
entries.use_for: Private RAG API layer over local models for document Q&A
entries.why: OpenAI-style API with ingestion, retrieval and chat over local models, a ready backend for private document assistants.
entries.summary: Open-source API layer that turns local models into production AI applications, offering ingestion, retrieval and chat primitives with an API modeled on the Claude API. Powers Zylon's on-premise AI platform.
entries.best_for: Building private, on-premise document assistants and RAG backends without sending data to cloud APIs.
entries.not_for: A backend API rather than a polished end-user product; you bring or host local models and hardware.

entries.name: Qdrant
entries.use_for: Run a dedicated vector database with payload filtering for semantic and hybrid search.
entries.why: Fast Rust engine with strong metadata filtering, quantization and simple REST/gRPC APIs; easy to self-host or use as cloud.
entries.summary: Vector similarity search engine and database written in Rust, offering a service with REST and gRPC APIs. Stores points with payloads and supports extended filtering, quantization, and hybrid search.
entries.best_for: Dedicated, self-hosted or cloud vector database for semantic and hybrid search with strong metadata filtering.
entries.not_for: Another service to run; for small prototypes an embedded store (Chroma, LanceDB) or pgvector may be simpler.

entries.name: RAG-Anything
entries.use_for: All-in-one multimodal RAG over PDFs, images, tables and equations
entries.why: From the LightRAG team: parses mixed-content documents and builds a multimodal knowledge graph for retrieval in one pipeline.
entries.summary: Multimodal RAG framework built on LightRAG that parses documents containing text, images, tables and equations and builds a multimodal knowledge graph for retrieval in a single pipeline.
entries.best_for: RAG over PDFs and reports with figures, tables and formulas where text-only pipelines drop information.
entries.not_for: Heavier than text RAG (parsers plus vision/LLM calls); depends on LightRAG, so inherits graph-indexing cost.

entries.name: Ragent
entries.use_for: Fork a Java agentic RAG platform with hybrid retrieval, memory, MCP tools and an admin UI.
entries.why: Covers ingestion to answers with tracing, queueing and feedback, in plain Java.
entries.summary: Production-style Java Agentic RAG platform. It has hybrid retrieval with RRF and rerank, query rewriting and intent routing, session memory, model fallback, Redis queueing, MCP tools via AgentScope, ingestion pipelines and a back office.
entries.best_for: Java teams who want a complete RAG and agent reference to study or adapt.
entries.not_for: README and docs are in Chinese, and it is partly framed as interview learning. Not a drop-in library.

entries.name: RAGFlow
entries.use_for: Self-hosted RAG engine with deep document understanding and citation-grounded answers
entries.why: Most-starred open RAG engine; strong layout-aware parsing of PDFs/tables, deployable via Docker with an API.
entries.summary: Open-source RAG engine combining deep document understanding with agent capabilities. Parses layout-heavy PDFs and tables, produces citation-grounded answers, deploys via Docker and exposes an API.
entries.best_for: A self-hosted RAG product with strong layout-aware parsing and citations for enterprise knowledge bases.
entries.not_for: A full application stack with notable resource needs (Docker, several services); not a lightweight library to embed.

entries.name: RuVector
entries.use_for: Give agents persistent local memory with vector search and graph links.
entries.why: One Rust core usable from Rust, Node, Python, the browser and MCP.
entries.summary: A Rust-native store for agent memory and vector retrieval. It combines local embeddings, persistent vectors, graph relations and feedback learning, with npm, PyPI and crates.io packages and an MCP server.
entries.best_for: Local-first agent memory or vector search that must run in Node, Rust, Python or the browser.
entries.not_for: A large sprawling project with many sub-packages. Check which package fits before you adopt it.

entries.name: Sentence Transformers
entries.use_for: Compute text embeddings and rerank results with pretrained or fine-tuned models.
entries.why: The standard Python library for embedding and cross-encoder models, with thousands of compatible models on Hugging Face.
entries.summary: Python framework for computing embeddings with Sentence Transformer models, scoring with Cross-Encoder rerankers and generating sparse embeddings, with training support for all three. Works with thousands of models on Hugging Face.
entries.best_for: Generating embeddings, reranking results and fine-tuning embedding models in Python, with GPU support.
entries.not_for: Requires PyTorch (heavy install); for lightweight CPU-only embedding, FastEmbed is smaller. No vector storage.

entries.name: SentrySearch
entries.use_for: Search hours of video by text or image and get a trimmed clip back.
entries.why: Embeds video chunks directly, with cloud or fully local model options.
entries.summary: A CLI that splits video into overlapping chunks, embeds them with Gemini, Qwen cloud or a local Qwen3-VL model, and stores vectors in local ChromaDB. A text or image query returns the best match trimmed from the file.
entries.best_for: Finding moments in dashcam, security or other long footage without writing your own pipeline.
entries.not_for: Needs Python 3.11 or 3.12 and ffmpeg. The default backend needs a Gemini API key. A CLI, not a hosted service.

entries.name: sqlite-vec
entries.use_for: Add vector search to SQLite with a tiny, dependency-free extension
entries.why: Runs anywhere SQLite runs (incl. WASM, mobile); successor to sqlite-vss and the go-to for local-first vector search.
entries.summary: Very small SQLite extension in pure C with no dependencies for vector search. Stores float, int8 and binary vectors in vec0 virtual tables with metadata columns, runs anywhere SQLite does including WASM; successor to sqlite-vss.
entries.best_for: Local-first, mobile, browser or edge apps that need vector search inside SQLite.
entries.not_for: Pre-v1 with expected breaking changes; brute-force style search ('fast enough') rather than large-scale ANN indexes.

entries.name: TencentDB Agent Memory
entries.use_for: Share team memory across agents as chat memory, skills, an LLM wiki and a code graph.
entries.why: Turns conversations, docs and code into four reusable memory assets that are governed and shared.
entries.summary: A memory hub for AI agents that stores chat memory, skills, an LLM-built wiki and a code graph, and makes them available to several agents and frameworks such as OpenClaw and Hermes. It is installed from npm and includes a migration tool for older versions.
entries.best_for: Teams running several agents that keep repeating the same context and work.
entries.not_for: Team Memory is in beta and moving fast. License is listed as unclear (NOASSERTION) on GitHub; check before building on it.

entries.name: turbovec
entries.use_for: Compressed vector index using TurboQuant quantization
entries.why: Rust ANN index with Python bindings built on TurboQuant, giving high recall at a fraction of FAISS-style memory.
entries.summary: In-process vector index for Python and Rust that stores each vector at 2 or 4 bits per dimension using TurboQuant and searches the compressed form with SIMD kernels. README claims 10M 768-d embeddings fit in 4 GB.
entries.best_for: Memory-constrained, large embedding sets needing a compressed in-process index with high recall.
entries.not_for: In-process index library, not a database service; the README has its own 'when to use something else' section, and the project is new.

entries.name: txtai
entries.use_for: All-in-one embeddings database for semantic search, RAG and LLM workflows
entries.why: Single package combining vector index, SQL, graph and pipelines; lightweight alternative to running a separate vector DB.
entries.summary: All-in-one AI framework centered on an embeddings database that combines sparse and dense vector indexes, graph networks and relational databases. Supports semantic search with SQL, RAG, agents and multi-model workflows.
entries.best_for: Single-package semantic search and RAG where you want vector index, SQL and graph without a separate vector DB.
entries.not_for: Opinionated all-in-one stack, so less flexible than assembling best-of-breed parts; Python only.

entries.name: Unstructured
entries.use_for: Partition and chunk messy documents (PDF, HTML, email, Office) into elements for LLMs
entries.why: Widely used ingestion layer with partitioning and chunking strategies; integrated into LangChain and LlamaIndex.
entries.summary: Open-source components for ingesting and pre-processing images and documents (PDF, HTML, Word, email, Office) into structured elements and chunks for LLMs, with connectors and partitioning strategies; integrated with LangChain and LlamaIndex.
entries.best_for: Normalizing messy mixed-format documents into elements and chunks before embedding.
entries.not_for: Best accuracy on hard PDFs requires heavier models or the paid API; dependencies can be large. Docling is an alternative for layout-heavy PDFs.

entries.name: Utopia
entries.use_for: Stand up an offline knowledge base with a bitemporal graph and ontology instead of plain RAG.
entries.why: Tracks how knowledge changes over time, so past decisions can be traced to their grounds.
entries.summary: An enterprise knowledge system written in Rust. It builds a bitemporal knowledge graph that keeps time and ontology at the base, detects conflicts, and routes doubtful cases to human review. It deploys offline on hardware you control.
entries.best_for: Organizations that need auditable, evolving knowledge with an audit trail for agent decisions.
entries.not_for: Every use case needs a chat model configured. The marketing-heavy README gives little API detail, so check maturity first.

entries.name: Weaviate
entries.use_for: Run a vector database that stores objects plus vectors with built-in hybrid search and vectorizer modules.
entries.why: Combines BM25 and vector search out of the box and can call embedding models for you; mature clients for Python, TS, Go and Java.
entries.summary: Cloud-native vector database that stores objects and vectors with hybrid (BM25 plus vector) search, filtering, reranking and RAG in one query interface. Can vectorize at import via integrated model modules.
entries.best_for: Production semantic and hybrid search where you want built-in vectorizers and mature clients (Python, TS, Go, Java).
entries.not_for: Heavier to run than embedded stores; schema/collection concepts add learning curve for small prototypes.

entries.name: WeKnora
entries.use_for: Document understanding and RAG framework for building knowledge-base Q&A
entries.why: Tencent RAG stack: multimodal parsing, hybrid retrieval and agentic reasoning, deployable as a service with a web UI.

license_verified.note: LICENSE states WeKnora is licensed under MIT; bundled third-party components keep their own licenses

entries.summary: LLM-powered framework for enterprise document understanding and knowledge-base Q&A. Offers multimodal parsing, hybrid retrieval, an agent with skills and a wiki, deployable as a service with a web UI.
entries.best_for: Standing up a team knowledge base with RAG, agent and wiki features as a self-hosted service.
entries.not_for: A full service with web UI rather than a small library; stack and docs are Tencent-centric, so check maturity before depending on it.

entries.name: zvec
entries.use_for: Lightweight in-process vector database embedded in your app
entries.why: Alibaba-built embedded vector DB: SQLite-style, no server to run, fast ANN search for local and edge RAG.
entries.summary: Lightweight in-process vector database from Alibaba that embeds directly into applications SQLite-style with no server. Battle-tested internally, with low-latency similarity search; recent releases add a zvec-grep local search CLI.
entries.best_for: Embedded or edge vector search for local RAG without running a separate server.
entries.not_for: In-process only, so no standalone multi-client server; young project with fast-moving versions (v0.x).
